headline: Bitcoin holds near $81,700 after record-size ETF outflow; oil tops $101
summary: U.S. stocks closed lower Thursday: the Nasdaq fell 2.6% (its worst day since June) and the S&P 500 1.2% (its worst since July), led by Meta, AMD and Amazon on doubts about the payoff from heavy AI spending; early Friday, S&P 500 futures are roughly flat, Nasdaq futures are up about 0.25% and Dow futures down about 0.2%. At about 6:30 a.m. bitcoin is near $81,700 (down 0.3% over 24 hours) and ether near $2,400, after spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $635 million Thursday, their biggest one-day outflow since June; total crypto value is down about 2.9% to $2.73 trillion, the Fear & Greed index is 50 (Neutral), and the meme coin PEPE is up about 11%. The TSX closed down 1%, U.S. crude is up 1.6% to about $101 with Brent near $114 on Middle East supply fears, gold is near $4,037, and the 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.95–4.97% after its biggest one-day fall since March 2023.

crypto.label: Risk-off
crypto.why: Bitcoin and ether are flat over 24 hours, but total crypto value is down about 2.9%, spot bitcoin ETFs had their largest outflow since June on Thursday, and the Fear & Greed index has slid from 68 (Greed) to 50 (Neutral) in a day.

stocks.label: Risk-off
stocks.why: The Nasdaq closed down 2.6% and the S&P 500 1.2%, with Meta and AMD down 7–8% and the VIX fear gauge near 19.6; futures are mixed early Friday and investors are still favouring Treasuries.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta closed down 7% at $648.85 even after beating forecasts, as investors weigh its $135–$145 billion spending plan, negative free cash flow and a new non-voting share class; AMD fell 8.1%, Amazon 4.6%, Nvidia and Broadcom about 4.3–4.4%, and Lam Research about 9% after its results. A report that Nvidia and Tesla plan to invest in a Samsung supplier revived worries about 'circular' AI deals, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other.
drivers.assets: Nasdaq, chip stocks, Shopify, Celestica, bitcoin

drivers.title: Stablecoin rules finalized
drivers.detail: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a top U.S. bank regulator, finalized reserve, redemption and risk rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027. Crypto stocks rallied on it Wednesday, but Coinbase and Strategy gave back about 4.5% and 5% Thursday with bitcoin.

drivers.title: Bond yields tumble as investors seek safety
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 19 basis points (0.19 percentage point) Thursday to near 4.95–4.97%, its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, as investors fled to safety. Traders trimmed bets on Fed tightening: a December rate hike is no longer fully priced (about 85% odds), though the Fed is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28.

drivers.title: Oil tops $101 despite U.S. supply push
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 1.6% to $101 a barrel early Friday and Brent is near $114, a five-month high and up about 4% this week, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and reports that the U.S. and Israel are drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran; a move by President Trump to invoke a Cold War-era law to boost fuel production has not cooled prices. Higher oil feeds inflation fears, while gold is near $4,037 after a nearly 3% drop Thursday.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, bonds, crypto

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETFs post biggest outflow since June
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $1.08 billion over the prior three days, then lost about $635 million on Thursday, the largest one-day outflow since June 25 per SoSoValue data, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. About $406 million of leveraged crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, per CoinGlass.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada expected to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased, and economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28. Hopes for progress in Canada–U.S. trade talks helped the TSX to a four-week high Wednesday.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 0.3% in 24h and 0.7% this week, at about $81,730 (down 5.0% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, briefly breaking above the $84,000 ceiling that had stopped it on Oct. 13–14, then fell back below $82,000 overnight as Tesla's and Meta's results revived doubts about AI spending; it held near $81,000–$81,700 as the Nasdaq closed down 2.6%. The round trip caused about $458 million of liquidations over the day (leveraged bets closed automatically), about 91% of them bullish bets, per CoinGlass data cited by The Crypto Times. Bitcoin's share of total crypto value is near 59.5%, close to its highest since May, as traders shelter in it while smaller coins fall harder. Overnight it dipped below $81,000 before recovering toward $82,000 in Asian trading, where it is testing its 50-day average; SoSoValue data show spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $635 million on Thursday, their biggest single-day outflow since June 25, ending three days of inflows worth about $1.08 billion.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is now trading closely with tech stocks, and it is sitting just above the $80,000 floor of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $75,000 or lower.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A further slide in tech stocks, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: Whether the Nasdaq steadies Friday (futures are mixed early), the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, whether Thursday's large ETF outflows continue, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 0.3% in 24h and 2.4% this week, at about $2,401 (down 12% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back and is hovering just above the $2,400 level that had held as support for about a week, after dipping under it Thursday. It keeps trailing bitcoin as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $2,400, ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Staying below $2,400 with continued ETF outflows could send it toward the $2,300 area, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, and the ETH/BTC ratio.

crypto.name: Pepe
crypto.move: Up 11% in 24h and 20% this week, at about $0.00000502 (flat over 30 days); trending on CoinGecko
crypto.why: PEPE, the largest frog-themed meme coin (a token with no product, driven by online hype), is the biggest gainer among large coins today. There is no official news behind it: on Oct. 21 it had the biggest jump in trading activity on South Korean exchanges relative to normal, and futures trading has been running at more than five times spot trading, with open interest (the value of open bets) near $270 million, per CoinMarketCap's summary of market data.
crypto.meaning: Gains built on borrowed money and a burst of retail trading in one region can unwind fast if those bets are closed. PEPE is still far below its December 2024 record, and meme coins tend to swing much more than bitcoin in both directions.

outlook.bullCase: If meme-coin interest keeps building and bitcoin holds $80,000, PEPE could extend toward the $0.0000055–$0.000006 area.
outlook.bearCase: A wider crypto sell-off or a wave of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically) could erase the week's gain and send it back toward $0.0000041–$0.0000044.
outlook.watch: Futures open interest and funding rates, Korean exchange volume, and whether bitcoin holds $80,000.

crypto.name: AKEDO
crypto.move: Up 16% in 24h and 3.8% this week, at about $0.0329 (down 21% over 30 days)
crypto.why: AKEDO is a small AI-tools token that has just squeezed into CoinGecko's top 100. We could not find a clear news catalyst for the jump, which peaked overnight near $0.037, dropped about 14% in the hour to 3:25 a.m., and has since bounced back above $0.033; it comes two days after a scheduled Oct. 21 unlock of tokens worth about $63 million (roughly 9% of its market value), and after weeks stuck in a $0.029–$0.037 range. Earlier community analysis found the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, so a few holders can move the price sharply.
crypto.meaning: A double-digit jump on no identifiable news, in a token with extremely concentrated ownership, is the kind of move that can reverse just as quickly. The price was turned back at the old $0.037 ceiling, and anyone holding it is exposed to large holders and fresh unlocked supply.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $0.037 ceiling on steady volume would turn that level into support and could extend the move.
outlook.bearCase: Selling by large holders or recipients of the Oct. 21 unlock could send it back into the $0.029–$0.03 range or toward about $0.022, a level flagged as key support.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above about $0.03, trading volume, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and any official project news.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Down 6.7% in 24h and 9.7% this week, at about $183 (still up 148% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (Overledger) that connects banks' systems to blockchains. Its token soared after The Clearing House, a group owned by large U.S. banks, picked Quant on Sept. 24 to link systems for its plan to put bank deposits on blockchains. Since then it has been giving back gains through profit-taking and heavy leverage: it fell about 19% in the week to Oct. 20 and is sliding again with the altcoin sell-off.
crypto.meaning: The bank deal adds credibility, but it does not require banks to buy or hold the QNT token itself, so the price may have run ahead of what the deal means for token demand. After a gain this large, sharp swings in both directions are likely.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $170–$200 support zone and new details on bank pilots could bring a rebound toward $220–$250.
outlook.bearCase: A clean break below about $170 could extend the pullback toward $140–$150 as late buyers sell.
outlook.watch: The $170 level, futures open interest, and any updates from The Clearing House or Quant on the deposit-token project.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Down 8.7% in 24h but up 11% this week, at about $3.38 (down 35% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The token of the Lighter derivatives exchange jumped after reports from its Oct. 21 investor call that it plans to apply for a U.S. licence in November and is weighing access through Robinhood's U.S. platform; neither has been confirmed. outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.
outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or more profit-taking after Wednesday's 20% jump, could send it back toward about $3.20 or below.
outlook.watch: Official statements from Lighter, trading volume versus Hyperliquid, and token unlock schedules.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: Down 5.9% in 24h but up 8.0% this week, at about $609 (up 7.2% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, has slipped from about $650 late Wednesday to near $608, one of the bigger drops among large coins over the past day, though it is still up about 9% on the week. We found no project-specific news behind the pullback (the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance), so it looks like the crowded leveraged trade unwinding as the wider market cooled. The run had started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading had outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, with funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) near 70% a year, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $600 line, futures open interest and funding rates (falling funding would mean the leverage is clearing out), spot versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 3.0% in 24h and 0.4% this week, at about $1,217 (down 24% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Today those leveraged bets are unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders are closing positions, and the price has fallen about 11% to just above the $1,190–$1,230 support area.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and today shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Down 1.3% in 24h and 6.3% this week, at about $4.93 (up 8.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: A further unwinding of leveraged bets, or the proposal stalling, could take it toward $4.50 or below; it has now slipped back under $5.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether it can get back above $5.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 0.2% in 24h and 2.4% this week, at about $104.30 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and is down about 4% as altcoins slide.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin break below $80,000, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000–$85,000 range, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Closed down 1.2% at 7,663 Thursday, about 2.3% below its record near 7,845
stocks.why: The index slid through the session as Meta, AMD, Amazon and Nvidia fell on renewed doubts about returns from AI spending, while oil near $100 revived inflation worries. Apple (up 1.2% to a record) and JPMorgan (up 0.4%) cushioned the drop, the Dow ended flat, and the VIX fear gauge rose about 14% to 19.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether the 7,600 area holds Friday, oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening; overnight, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are only about 0.1–0.2% lower, per Reuters.

stocks.meaning: The AI trade bounced Wednesday, but heavy overnight selling in Asian tech, with Chinese tech shares in Hong Kong having their worst day since April 2025, shows investors are nervous about how much Big Tech is spending on AI and when it pays off.

outlook.bullCase: Upbeat AI revenue and spending commentary from Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet could carry it back toward the 27,500–27,700 highs.
outlook.bearCase: If today's losses extend, the 26,000 level could give way, with the 25,500 area the next stop; disappointing cloud results next week would add pressure.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds 26,000 on Friday, the chip-stock losing streak, Alphabet and Microsoft on Oct. 28, and Treasury yields; overnight, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are only about 0.1–0.2% lower, per Reuters.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 7% at $648.85 Thursday after touching $639.69, from $697.52 Wednesday
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock fell as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly. Meta's filing says the Class C dividend is expected to work like a two-for-one stock split for Class A holders.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it below Thursday's low near $640 toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether Thursday's low near $640 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Closed down 8.1% at $507.93 Thursday, about 23% below its 52-week high

Intel is down 4–5%, Nvidia about 4.4%, and Lam Research about 9% after its own results. stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.
outlook.watch: Chip-sector moves, Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29, and AMD's Nov. 3 results.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed down 3.1% at $374.58 Thursday, near the day's low of $373.71
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but it slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened and closed near the day's low.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $374 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: Strategy
stocks.move: Closed down 5% at $145.80 Thursday, giving back most of Wednesday's 7.5% gain
stocks.why: Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder with about 848,000 BTC, tends to move two to three times as much as bitcoin. stocks.meaning: MSTR is effectively a leveraged bet on bitcoin, so it amplifies both gains and losses. Its moves today say more about bitcoin than about the company.

stocks.name: Shopify
stocks.move: Closed down 3.5% at C$236.41 Thursday after touching C$231.75, about 8% below its high
stocks.why: Shopify is falling with U.S. tech stocks. It had climbed about 25% over the past month as investors bet on strong holiday-season sales, and there is no company-specific news today.
stocks.meaning: Shopify is Canada's biggest tech stock and moves with U.S. tech sentiment. After a big run, expectations for its next results are high.

outlook.bullCase: Strong megacap earnings and early holiday-spending signals could push it through C$256 to new highs.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech pullback could drag it toward the C$225–C$230 area, where it traded in early October.
outlook.watch: Nasdaq direction, consumer-spending data, and its upcoming results.

stocks.name: TD Bank
stocks.move: Closed flat at C$175.14 Thursday after hitting a new 52-week high of C$175.99
stocks.why: Canadian banks are holding up while the rest of the market falls, as investors expect the Bank of Canada to keep its rate at 2.25% on Oct. 28; core inflation measures eased in September even as headline inflation rose to 3.1%. Steady rates support bank lending margins, and lower bond yields make bank dividends look more attractive.
stocks.meaning: TD is near a record, so the next leg depends on a stable rate outlook and its next results. Bank stocks are a big part of many Canadian portfolios.

outlook.bullCase: A steady Bank of Canada and calm credit markets could take TD through C$175 to new highs.
outlook.bearCase: A surprise hawkish turn or credit worries could pull it back to the C$167–C$170 area.
outlook.watch: The Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Canadian Natural Resources
stocks.move: Closed down 0.9% at C$75.50 Thursday after touching a new 52-week high of C$77.60 at the open
stocks.why: Canada's largest oil producer hit a new high at the open as U.S. crude neared $100 and Brent reached about $112, its highest since May, after attacks on Saudi energy sites and reports of possible renewed U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran. It then gave back the gain as the whole TSX fell.
stocks.meaning: CNQ's fortunes track oil prices closely, so it can hold up even if the wider TSX opens lower.

outlook.bullCase: Continued Middle East tension keeping Brent above $105 could push CNQ past today's high of C$77.60.
outlook.bearCase: A credible Iran deal that sends oil sharply lower would hit CNQ, possibly back toward C$70–C$72.
outlook.watch: Iran–U.S. talks, Brent crude, and weekly U.S. oil inventories.

newCoins.name: Pearl

newCoins.why: It is trending on CoinGecko and in the top 100 at about $2.11: down about 13% today after touching a record near $2.46, but still up about 12% this week and 35% over 30 days, riding the 'useful AI mining' story.
newCoins.redFlags: A researcher found the main mining software contained no actual AI code, and a co-founder admitted miners can 'spam mine'. Supply grows by about 1 million tokens a day, roughly doubling over the next year. It trades on very few exchanges with thin liquidity.
